   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  November 14, 2024

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:09 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Esquivel

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Executive Assistant
Present: Chair Flores, Vice Chair Lizette Ruiz, Secretary Edgar Pelayo and Commissioner Esquivel.
Commissioner Alejanda Flores had an excused absence.
Staff: Director of Parks & Recreation Steve Costley, Deputy Director Tina Fierro, and Parks Superintendent
Glenn Massey.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES FOR SEPTEMBER 12, 2024
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Esquivel to approve the minutes as presented.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, expressed his displeasure that the new Parks Master Plan hasn’t begun.

PRESENTATION - None

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. REVIEW OF RECREATION PROGRAMS 1ST QUARTER FY 2024/25
Recommended Motion: Motion approve receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Esquivel
Deputy Dir. Fierro reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Commissioner Esquivel asked if there could be
more than one Family Camp Out and have teens included. Vice Chair Ruiz is happy with the Parks’ events,
especially with the Cultural events. Secretary Pelayo asked if the Department could do fund raising to fund
events. Deputy Dir. Fierro explained that staff does ask for sponsorships. Director Costley explained that
the Parks & Recreation Department has at most a 50% recovery rate; it is not a money making department.
Secretary Pelayo asked if there is a noticeable increase in with social media? Chair Flores said good job and
asked to look for sponsors at small business too.

2. REVIEW OF GROUNDS & FACILITY MAINTENANCE 1ST QUARTER FY 2024/25
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Secretary Pelayo
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, is not happy with lack of improvements at Triangle Park;
wants more trees and more seating.
Vice Chair Ruiz said the batting cages keep breaking down, can Sofive repair more of them? Also, swings
are missing in the playground and could more toddler swings be installed. At the Gardendale Tot Lot there
is sand in the play area which is very dirty with cat feces. Can CDBG monies be used to repair equipment?
Director Costley explained that those monies are for lower income areas in the City and Hollydale doesn’t
qualify. Parks Supt. Massey will speak with PW Staff about the equipment and to Grounds staff about
routinely cleaning the sand.

  Page 1 of 3
  4
 Commissioner Esquivel asked if the batting cages are being repaired? Deputy Dir. Fierro has spoken with
them; they are looking for funding to replace all of them.
Chair Flores asked which park has the most problem with gophers? Parks Supt. Massey said Hollydale
Regional Park and the Westside area parks.

3. DESIRED OUTCOMES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025/26
Recommended Motion: Motion to provide input to the Parks & Recreation Department regarding desired
outcomes for the next fiscal year.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, wants to know when the splash pads will be installed.
Vice Chair Ruiz asked if pickle ball will be an annual event? Deputy Dir. Fierro replied possibly in March.
When the construction concludes at Circle Park it will have pickle ball courts. Perhaps also dual use of the
Tennis Courts. Secretary Pelayo asked if social media was used as a way to survey as to the communities
comments on events and what they suggest for future activities/events. Grandparents Day was
postponed, perhaps concentrate on more flyers; noticed the Concerts in the Park feature Spanish music.
Deputy Dir. Fierro staff has tried English music and the community preferred Spanish. Commissioner
Esquivel mentioned the bleachers at Diamonds 9 & 10 are very bad; the wooden one gives people splinters
and the metal ones are cut and unsafe. Director Costley will have staff go out and check them and look into
funding for new bleachers. Commissioner Esquivel asked about the costs for a splash pad; Director Costley
said it would cost about $1.5 million to start, then there would be all the maintenance supplies and costs.
Chair Flores suggested being more aggressive at the department’s booths at events to attract more people.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Our Secretary, Reyna Gutierrez will retire after 23 years with us, and we lost our
Marketing Coordinator. We are short a Transit, Fitness, and two Recreation Coordinators; staff is working
with HR to fill those positions. The Maintenance divisions are fully staffed. The fencing project has been
completed, Hollydale Community Park has a new contractor and estimate a grand opening in January;
Circle Park demo is completed, and the contractor is working on the infrastructure with a completion date
of March; has a meeting regarding the Urban Orchard on Monday, possibly a five month project. The
mural at the water tower is almost completed. Invited the Commission to the Pageant of the Trees on
December 7.

Deputy Dir. Fierro: Art Walk was in October, next year is the 10 year anniversary hoping for something
different. Trunk or Treat event at City Hall; won 3rd place in decorations, Patti’s Pumpkin Plunge was
successful. Halloween was revamped and was very successful. The Veteran’s Day ceremony was very nice.
Tomorrow is the 2nd Family Night with a reptile show. Next week are the Department’s dance recitals. Staff
is preparing for Winter Wonderland the week following we’ll be assisting the PD with Pageant of the Trees.
The Christmas Parade will be December 8 and it will be down Southern. Director Costley asked the
Commissioners to help spread the word to the community of the change. Breakfast with Santa is on
December 14.

Parks Supt. Massey: Maintenance Staff will be busy assisting with all the upcoming special events. And
winterizing plants and adjusting the sprinklers at all City parks. Chair Flores asked what staff is doing to
prepare Southern for the parade. Grounds staff takes care of everything west of California; Public Works is
responsible for the rest.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS – Secretary Pelayo asked if the Master Plan bids can be
brought back to the Commission. Director Costley replied that the request for proposal is on the City’s
website; staff will bring back the top three for their review. Chair Flores asked for a report on the items
that will be taken to Council on the changing the sand to turf; changing the bleachers; something can be
brought back to the December meeting.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Parks & Recreation Director
Date:  November 26, 2024

Subject:  Review Of Goals and Performance Measures for Fiscal Year 2025-26

Recommended Motion: Approve the proposed Goals and Performance Measures for
fiscal year 2025-26 and present to Council.

Report Summary: Each year the Parks & Recreation Department staff prepares goals
and performance measures that will direct work and support budget requests for the
coming fiscal year. This process assists staff, the Commission and Council to have a
unified vision of desired outcomes that the City will attempt to achieve through the work
of the department for that fiscal year.

Our goal for this meeting is to keep the Commission informed on what the plans are for
the Department moving into FY25/26 and allow them to discuss any areas of concern for
the Parks & Recreation Department as we move forward into the City’s budget process.

Once the Goals & Performance measures are approved by Commission, the department
staff will begin the process of completing the financial part of the budget program so that
all of the funding for the department reflects the desired outcomes for the new fiscal year.

Attachment: Goals and Performance Measures for FY 2025-26

   CONTRACT CLASSES
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION
The City of South Gate’s Parks and Recreation department offers a variety of classes and
programs that help enrich the community. The classes and programs that are offered create a
foundation for the public to establish new skills or freshen up on skills. These classes and
programs are essential to the community because of the positive impact they create on members
of the community by building up their self-esteem, reducing loneliness, and enhancing overall
health and well-being.

Prior Year’s Accomplishments FY 2024-25:
  • Offered 1 new youth contract class with 15 registered participants per class.
  • Offered 1 new adult contract class with 15 registered participants per class.
  • Offered (2) 1-day workshops for adults.

Goals & Objectives for FY 2025-26:
  • Re-vamp quarterly dance recitals.

   SPORTS CENTER
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION
Our fitness program offers four types of memberships (Sports, Sports & Splash, Fitness, Premier).
Premier members have access to the fitness center, free-weight room, group exercise classes,
racquetball courts, basketball gym, and swimming pool. Fitness members have access to
everything above except the swim stadium, but both Premier and Fitness have the option of
purchasing personal training sessions and/or registering for a Biggest Loser Challenge. Specialty
programs and training sessions have a separate fee in addition to the Premier and Fitness
membership fees. Sports and Splash members have access to the swimming pool and basketball
gym. Lastly, Sports members only have access to the basketball gym.

   AQUATICS
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION:
Aquatics encompass a range of recreational, fitness and competitive activities that are presented
at the Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium. Included in this are open recreational swim times,
fitness lap swimming, adults only sessions, swim lessons, and pool rentals. This program also
supports our Swim Team and Youth Water polo program as well as programs from several local
high schools.

  of their $25,000 grant.
  •  Offered Community CPR/First Aid/AD classes with over 15 registrants.
  •  Hosted 4 USA Swimming meets in partnership with SGAC, including a prestigious “Last
  Ditch” meet.
  •  Had over 20 private rentals, including graduation parties, birthday parties, baptisms,
  and film rentals.
  •  Hosted a number of special events, including a Water Safety Bash,
  World's Largest Swim Lesson, Community Swim Days, Patti’s Pumpkin Plunge, and
  Surfing with Santa.

  ahead of the busy summer season. Spring 2026.

   ADULT SPORTS
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION
Our Adult Sports section currently provides programming that includes leagues, drop-in activities
and special events. Our current league play includes the following: Men’s softball, Co-ed softball,
Women’s Softball, Men’s basketball, Women’s basketball (starting soon), Wooden Bat Baseball

Men’s and Women’s basketball is hosted on Friday evenings. The wooden and metal baseball
leagues are held on Sunday’s. Open-Play Volleyball is our current drop-in program for adults, we
see a consistent average of about 225 participants monthly. Lastly, we offer Adult Sports special
events, which provide a variety of opportunities for adults to compete, stay active and have fun.

   GOLF COURSE

PROGRAM DESCRIPTION
This activity provides for the maintenance, operation and programming at the City’s 9-hole par 3

concessions. The course is open seven days a week from 8:00 a.m. till dusk.

Prior Year’s Accomplishments FY 2024-25:

  • Relocated Hole 1 to its original location

Report Summary: The following is a report of accomplishments performed by the
Grounds Division during 2024. The report will identify completed goals and objectives
outside of our ongoing routine parks maintenance.

❖ Ground Maintenance staff planted multiple flats of Gazania plants at City Hall near
  the water department entrance and twenty Azaleas were replaced inside the Azalea
  Garden at the Senior Center.

❖ We replaced 10 drinking fountains throughout South Gate Park from a company
  called, “Most Dependable Drinking Fountains.”

❖ Work continues with the turf reseeding program to fill in various bare spots and
  encourage strong turf growth throughout City parks.

❖ We hope to trim some of the larger trees at Hollydale Regional Park by year’s end.
  Staff are working with Tree People of Los Angeles to complete a tree grant, with the
  goal of planting approximately 200 trees at South Gate Park and westside parks.

❖ Over 110 irrigation valves were repaired and 78 were replaced. Approximately 825
  irrigation sprinkler heads were replaced at all parks. Over the past year staff have
  repaired approximately 90 lateral irrigation lines and 40 mainline irrigation pipes. We
  assisted the fence contractor moving irrigation mainlines and lateral pipes ahead of
  the installation of concrete mow strips.

❖ One large French drain was installed near the picnic shelters on the north side of
  South Gate Park.

❖ Two ball washers were replaced at the Golf Course and two new sand bunkers were
